subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram slash sessions still resolve to channel=(unknown), causing elevated allowFrom checks to fail on 2026.3.13

question: Should OpenClaw accept and normalize bare `telegram:slash:<id>` session keys for sandbox/elevated diagnostics, and if so which linked fix shape should become canonical?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the repair affects channel identity used by elevated host-exec authorization and there are already open linked fork candidates with different approaches.

options.title: Adopt a narrow canonical fix
options.body: Review or replace the linked fork candidates with a focused fix for bare Telegram slash-session channel identity plus regression coverage and redacted live Telegram proof.

options.title: Require agent-scoped diagnostics only
options.body: Close the product contract around `agent:<id>:telegram:*` diagnostics and update docs/error text so bare slash keys are not expected to authorize elevated checks.

options.title: Wait for contributor proof
options.body: Keep the issue paired to the open fork PRs until a maintainer can review their proof and decide whether either branch is safe to adopt.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow canonical fix
recommendation.body: Review or replace the linked fork candidates with a focused fix for bare Telegram slash-session channel identity plus regression coverage and redacted live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for sandbox explain and session-key diagnostics points to steipete’s original and follow-up work in this area.
